text: Just because you understand someone, you hear someone, doesn't mean that you have to agree with that person. But let me tell you, it is a different world in terms of the relationship when you can see the person for who they are and what they think and what they're saying. When you can genuinely leave your world and go into theirs and hear them, then the disagreement is not personal. The disagreement is not bitter and resentful. It's wholesome. It's I hear you.
title: Hearing Isn't Agreeing
broll: Two people talking on a park bench, one listening intently, long lens
Hand resting on a friend's shoulder, warm window light
Two paths that meet in a forest clearing, drone

shiur: Remarks at OJC-CCJ Yom Hashoa Memorial 2025
text: To be good to a righteous level means that we have to get out of bed in the morning for that purpose. We have to make it the aim of our life. We have to choose it. Choose good. Again. And again. And again. Every day. But here's the thing. It's not easy to be evil either. It's easy to be mediocre.
title: It's Easy to Be Mediocre
hook: It's Not Easy to Be Good.
broll: Alarm clock at dawn, a hand switching it off and rising
Runner on an empty road at first light
Sunrise breaking over a hilltop, time-lapse

text: We live on the dependency of other people around us, which never works because you know why? You can't control other people. No one can. Think about how hard it is to control ourselves. We can barely control ourselves and we believe that we can control other people. It is a waste of time, a withering away of our whole being, and yet we incessantly manipulate, undermine, passive-aggressive, insult, slander, shame, just so that we can get a bit of a leg up, which never lasts and is valueless in the long run.
title: You Can't Control People
broll: Puppet strings hanging slack in a dark theatre
Sand slipping through fingers, macro
Kite pulling free in the wind

text: What do we define as being beautiful? Beauty is when we find all of the details that we're aware of, find their perfect place in relation with every other detail. So if you look at an eyebrow, right, on its own, it could be a very ugly thing. But when it's on the face of a gorgeous model, it's a very different thing, right? Why? Because the other eyebrow is just in the right proportion to that one, the nose is just in perfect proportion to those, and the eyes are just in proportion to those, and so on. And so it's not just an eye and a nose, it's how they work together.
title: What Beauty Is
broll: Mosaic tiles fitting together, macro
Orchestra instruments in harmony, close-ups
Sunlight across a symmetrical stone archway

shiur: Raising Jewish Children ICZ Community Zurich 2022
text: We don't struggle to control ourselves, but we think we can control everybody else. And we cannot control other people. We cannot control our children. And we think we can make them something. You cannot make your children anything. What you can do is support them and give them the tools and the resources and all that they need for the best of your ability to be what they will be. you can encourage them, you can advise them, you cannot make them be something. And once we accept that truth, life gets to be much easier for us and much more pleasant because we cannot control it.
title: You Can't Make Your Children Anything
broll: Parent watching a child ride a bike away, from behind
Small hands planting a seedling
Young tree tied to a support stake in a garden

text: We will stop playing games because we are not prepared to hear the results If I won't win, I won't play If I can't play good enough, I won't engage We get to points in our lives where we are so afraid of vulnerability we will not even allow ourselves to play games anymore But when we stop playing we lose all really the joy that we have and just being able to be in life for the sake of life. We lose the enjoyment of just being able to go with the flow as life would have it. And the worst situations are when we really close ourselves off to the point where we can't even play cards without it being a serious endeavor.
title: Why We Stop Playing
broll: Kids laughing in a sprinkler, slow motion
Deck of cards scattered on a kitchen table
Adult swinging on a playground swing at sunset

shiur: Remarks at OJC-CCJ Yom Hashoa Memorial 2025
text: On Yom HaShoah, we of course pause to remember the suffering and the horror of the perishing of six million of our brothers and sisters. But we must also on Yom HaShoah pause to remember that the evil that killed them, murdered them, was human. It was human. And I believe that it is a mistake to consider it anything other than that.
title: The Evil Was Human
broll: Memorial candle flame in darkness
Railway tracks disappearing into fog, black and white
Stones placed on a memorial, macro

text: You know the broken window concept, right? That you have a broken window in a neighborhood that's not fixed, crime rates go up because it is a loud and clear signal that nobody's watching and nobody cares. And that's all you need. I used to say that to my teachers all the time in the school. You think that this is a minor thing. You think that your classroom being clean is a minor thing. You think that a homework being missed is a minor thing. It's not a minor thing. It's a broken window.
title: The Broken Window
broll: Single broken window in an old brick building
Clean, ordered classroom in morning light
Hand straightening a picture frame

shiur: Abraham's Covenant and the Miracle of Hanuka YUStern 2022
text: There is a familial bond that holds you all together. Because it may very well be that you don't particularly like everyone in your family. You may like to hang out with other people more. But you know that if they needed you, you would probably be on the first train, plane, car, back to wherever it was that they were and you'd be there and do what it is that they needed from you. There's a very big difference between like and familial bond. And it is something that we take for granted, that it will always be there. We take for granted in our own families and we take it for granted in our broader national family that is us.
title: Liking vs. Family
hook: You Don't Have to Like Them.
broll: Family around a crowded holiday table, laughing
Train pulling into a station at night
Old family photo album pages turning

text: What are you saying to yourself about yourself all the time? And I would say this to you First of all, pay attention to it Listen to it So the next time that you forget your keys Or you forgot to call someone Or you didn't respond to the emails in time Or whatever it is You start berating yourself internally Stop And think this If you had a child In your care That made the same mistake that you did Or intentionally did the same thing That you did How would you parent that child? Would you speak to the child the way that you speak to you? Chances are it would be child abuse if you did.
title: Would You Talk to a Child Like That?
hook: Would You Talk to a Child
the Way You Talk to Yourself?
broll: Woman looking into a fogged mirror, soft light
Parent kneeling to comfort a child
Keys left on a kitchen counter, macro

text: You can't be a free person if you're a creature of habit. You can't go and get the same paper every day and the same cup of coffee and the same route to work and be a free man. I'm not saying drive a different way to work. I'm not saying that. I'm saying that you can't do that and allow your brain to shut down. You have to constantly be conscious But you cannot take the same route to work every day and not be aware of what you're passing on the way You can't walk up the block of your house and not know every house on the block But people do, people don't even know how many steps they have to their house You walk up the steps every single day How many steps?
title: A Creature of Habit Isn't Free
broll: Commuters on the same route, time-lapse
Same coffee cup on the same desk each morning
Feet counting stone steps up to a front door

shiur: Understanding Prayer 1 - What is Prayer in Judaism Lauderdale Road 2024
text: Why do I consider humans to be conscious as opposed to any other of the animals that might be alive and aware on some level? Because when I say conscious, what I mean by that is that we are aware that we're aware, right? We have the ability to know that we know, which is really not shared in the same way with any other animal on the planet. It's very clear that that's the case because what human beings do with this awareness is vastly different to any other animal on the planet. So what that means is that we have the capacity to be able to ask the question, what if? And the only reason we have that capacity is because we have the ability to be aware that we're aware and consider what we think.
title: Aware That We're Aware
broll: Child looking up at a starry sky
Close-up of an eye opening in soft light
Person writing ‘what if?’ in a notebook, no face

text: How much time do you spend worrying about what is going to happen in the future? How much time do you spend anxious and worrying about what has happened in the past? More importantly, how much do those worries of future and past pull you out of the current moment of being in what is actually happening now? Because the only thing that we have is right now. How often does that happen for you? Try to answer that in your mind honestly. How much time is spent worrying about what will be, what has been, and how much does that pull you out of now, which is the only life that you and I have right here.
title: The Only Life Is Now
broll: Person sitting on a dock at a still lake at dawn
Clock hands blurred in motion
Steam rising from a cup of tea in morning light

text: We, the Jewish people, we are not the only ones who have suffered the ferocity, atrocity, horror of the human animal, but we have suffered it long, persistent, over and over and over again. And we should not be here. That's the reality. But here we are. And that is the single greatest miracle our people have ever seen. And we've had our share.
title: The Greatest Miracle
broll: Memorial candles flickering in darkness
Young people walking with Israeli flags at dusk, from behind
Sunrise over Jerusalem rooftops

text: We don't eat what we need to eat. We don't sleep what we need to sleep. We don't engage in the things that we need to when we need to. That's a master. A master is able to shut the book and go to sleep. We can't get, we get in bed and we think about 25 different things that are rushing through our head when we need to go to sleep. When we eat, we're reading the paper, we're talking to somebody, we're watching television, we're engaged in a conversation, we're having business meetings over our food.
title: Masters Can Stop
broll: Book being closed beside a bedside lamp
Single plate of food on a quiet table, no phone
Phone turned face down on a desk

shiur: Vayesheb Passing the Baton to Yosef
text: You have two choices in life You either have the choice to live in terms of relationship Or you have the choice to live in terms of jealousy And that's all there is If it's not relationship oriented, it's jealousy oriented Why? Because if it's relationship oriented Then you have a recognition of your place within the world Because you recognize where you fit in Literally, figuratively, and so on You have a place, you have an understanding of where you fit into everything And therefore there's never elements of jealousy because you never look at another person and say, oh that should be me. Because you know what's you. And that's not you. And that's it.
title: Relationship or Jealousy
broll: Two brothers walking in a field, from behind
Puzzle piece clicking into its place, macro
Two trees intertwined on a hillside

shiur: Shemot II. Sinai and the Giving of Torah
text: We are the most medicated human cohort in all of history because we're free. we finally got what we wanted and we're miserable. Now that doesn't mean that we're supposed to move backwards it's just being able to now deal with this and what it means to deal with it is to deal with our isolation to deal with the fact that no one else is going to live your life for you. You will be the only one responsible for living your life and you can numb it all you wish and you can run from it all all you wish, but you cannot hide from yourself.
title: The Most Medicated Generation
broll: Pharmacy shelves in cold fluorescent light
Person alone in a crowded city crossing
Mirror reflection in a dark room

shiur: Vaethanan Summer2018.Hope and Learning to Speak to the World
text: I mean, the first thing that you do a minute you leave home is what's the internet? What's the internet code? Literally, you can't even go to a restaurant without asking them what the internet code is. God forbid you should be offline for a few minutes. We can't tolerate being offline. I'm serious. That's not a joke. We really cannot. I mean, imagine being in a place where you don't have internet access. You think, oh, everybody says, oh, it'd be so wonderful. Yeah, bull. Please, give me a break. You'll get five minutes in and you're going to be ripping your hair out.
title: What's the Wi-Fi Code?
broll: Phone searching for signal in a remote landscape
Restaurant table with phones stacked face down
Empty mountain trail with no towers in sight

text: You want to go on a path that's good? It's in your hands. You want a path that's not good? It's in your hands. But don't for one minute pretend that you are something that you are not. You are human. You like to eat. You like to eat good food. You like to drink good things. You like to involve yourself socially with other people. When does it go wrong? I'll tell you when it goes wrong. It goes wrong when all you think about is your place, your little life, your little situation, and you need those things to be able to fill it.
title: It's in Your Hands
broll: Open hands catching morning light
Fork in a road at dawn
Hands shaping clay on a potter's wheel

text: You want your nervous system to stop judging? Not a pretty picture. No, the answer is not to stop judging. The answer is to become empathic. to learn to love. And from that judge for life, not for our own purposes. And you go from being judgmental to judicious. Judiciousness is life-giving. Judgmentalism is life-taking. It destroys everyone around it and the person that's doing it. So don't judge your friend until you get to their place. Not because you're wrong, necessarily. You could be absolutely right. But you're just going to destroy everything. Because you have absolutely no connection to what's going on.
title: Judicious, Not Judgmental
broll: Brass scales in dramatic side light
Two people embracing after an argument, silhouette
Seedling breaking through dry earth

shiur: On Reading Torah and Being - At Yavneh College 2015-10-12
text: How much do we really think about the fact that there is not another one of me in this world? And why is it important for us to think of that? It's important to think of it because there genuinely isn't. And if we came into this world and we have a life on this world, then there is something of value that we can bring to this world, just by way of our own being. And so the first thing that we have to do before we can love anybody else is to love ourselves. How do we love ourselves?
title: There's Only One of You
broll: Single snowflake on dark wool, macro
Fingerprint in ink, macro
One person in a vast landscape

text: We look at all this stuff, right? We look at it all. We rarely ever look at the person that is looking back at us in the mirror. Consider why. Well, it's weird. Why? It's intense. Well, it's just you. Try it for five minutes. It will seem like an eternity. Time it. If you've got a phone, put on a timer. Time it. And if five minutes is too much, do it for two. Let the water settle. Look at yourself in the eye. And consider how you feel about the person staring back at you.
title: Look Yourself in the Eye
broll: Still water settling in a basin
Phone timer counting down on a sink
Eye reflected in a mirror, close-up

text: We will exile them, relegate them into the dungeons of our souls, of our hearts. Those parts of ourselves that we are at odds with, that we do not feel comfortable with, that we do not find peace with, however it is that we feel about those parts of ourselves is how we will feel about people that represent those parts to us. So think carefully about the people that you do not like or cannot stand or wish you could just get rid of. They tell you something about how you feel about you.
title: The People You Can't Stand
broll: Shadowed staircase leading down to a cellar
Mirror cracked into many pieces
Door slowly opening into light

text: A question of what is it that you actually want? What's your desire? More often than not, your desire has a third party. Somebody's modeling it for you. You've seen what you want modeled in the world. Somebody else has what you want, and so you want what they want. Or you see that somebody else is experiencing, so you want what they experience. 99% of our desires comes from seeing these things modeled in the world. And the only question is, well, I mean, you know, think about who your models are. Which is why it is very, very important that we consider who it is that we hang out with.
title: Who Taught You to Want That?
broll: Shop window display with blurred passers-by
Scrolling social feed reflected in eyes
Child copying a parent's gesture

text: There's these two young fish that are swimming along in the sea, and then there's an old fish that's swimming their way and says to the two young fish, hey boys, how's the water? And they swim on and one fish turns to the other fish and he goes, what's water? And it's obviously pointing out the fact that you're in it. You don't even realize that you're in it. It's just what's around. So that's the first thing. The first thing is important to be able to understand, to be able to look from the outside for a minute at our society and what the nature of our society is.
title: What's Water?
broll: Fish swimming in clear blue water, underwater
Ripples spreading across a pond
Two young fish passing an older fish, underwater, soft light

text: Do you understand why nobody could live your life for you? It wouldn't mean anything if you couldn't achieve your own life. Does that mean that people fail sometimes? Yes, people fail. It's a real thing. I mean, it's not a game. Where it goes, it's okay, if you don't do it, I'll do it for you. No. If you don't do it, it's over. You missed it. But I'm not going to do it for you. You've got to do it yourself. So does that mean that I'm going to try to stand back and watch you make mistakes?
title: No One Can Live Your Life
broll: Lone hiker on a ridge at dawn
Hand writing in a journal by lamplight
Footprints on an empty beach

text: We are human beings, not human doings. That means first and foremost, our job as humans is to learn to be who it is that we are. and our whole lives should be dedicated to being who it is that we are. But we can get distracted from that tremendously by engaging so much in what it is that we're doing. And we do very often, all of us at one time or another have problem with this. At one time or another, we engage so much in doing in what it is that we're doing that we don't even remember why we started it in the first place.
title: Human Beings, Not Human Doings
broll: Overflowing to-do list on a desk, macro

shiur: What Does Being a Good Person Have to do with God and Judaism 2016
text: Most people do not love because you know what it takes for us to love? We are not pre-wired for love. We are pre-wired for security. and love requires a tremendous lack of security because of the vulnerabilities that it needs. You have to rip yourself open in order to be able to love someone genuinely. You have to be fully prepared to share everything that you are and all that you have with somebody if you're really going to love. Who's ready to do that? We work on it, we grow, there's trial and error. I mean, if we're being honest, that's the reality. So Avraham Avinu was ready to throw himself into the whole thing.
title: Wired for Security, Not Love
broll: Padlock on a bridge railing
Couple's hands slowly letting go and reaching again
Waves breaking against a sea wall

shiur: Adar, Ab and stepping happiness up and down
text: What's the biggest threat to losing this vision and living in this vision? Miracles. The worst possible thing that could happen. Why? Because what does a miracle tell me? Miracle tells me something's going wrong. God's got to come in and fix it. The world is not enough. The world that he created does not know how to self-correct. My GPS does, but the world doesn't. My GPS can recalculate if I make a wrong turn, right? The world falls apart. You got to call the technician to come in. Could you imagine if every time your GPS failed, you had to call somebody to come out and rewire your whole thing just to be able to get you where you're going?
title: Why Miracles Are a Threat

shiur: Vayikra 2022 - Bring in the blood and guts
text: I'm not just saying certain aspects of you that I find acceptable. No, I'm saying all of you, all of you, your aggression, your predatory nature, your lust, your dog-eat-dog survival drives, all of it, bring them into my house, and I will teach you how to channel those things into higher space. You do not need to amputate who you are to have a relationship with me. To the contrary. It's not the way to go. You need to embrace your humanity because I made your humanity. What do you think? Some other rival God made you?
title: Bring All of You

shiur: Tetsave - 2022 Stability of Mind - A lesson from the Kohen Gadol
text: Do you know how you wipe your mind clean? You control your thoughts. They don't control you. And one of the ways that you can start to do this, and like I said, it takes a tremendous amount of practice. This is what people call meditation in modern terms, but it's old, and we've been doing it for a long time, because what it does is it changes your mind, it changes and solidifies, it sturdies your mind the more you practice, and it protects it from the whims of all thoughts.
title: Wipe Your Mind Clean
broll: Still lake mirroring mountains at dawn
Chalkboard being wiped clean
Breath of steam in cold morning air

text: Start standing tall as God made you. If he wanted you to slouch and bend over, he would have made you an animal on all fours, or a primate of other sorts He made you a human being that stands upright, with your eyes facing forward, your head raised tall, not in arrogance Just walk as you are, and then start to get to know yourself Because in getting to know yourself, and that is a scary endeavor for many people, myself included There are parts that you don't know. There are parts that you've forgotten about. There are parts that you've sequestered into the dungeon so that they shouldn't bother your interactions that you are focused on.
title: Stand Tall
